evals.prompt: Define Cognitive Load Theory in 2-3 sentences. Include intrinsic, extraneous, and germane load.
expected_elements: Names working memory as limited
Defines intrinsic load as task difficulty or element interactivity
Defines extraneous load as presentation-caused unnecessary burden
Defines germane effort as schema-building work
Says the goal is not to remove all complexity

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model of Cognitive Load Theory using the RAM analogy. Name what intrinsic, extraneous, and germane load map to.
expected_elements: Working memory is a small workspace
Intrinsic load is the program or task that must run
Extraneous load is unnecessary background work
Germane effort is useful caching or schema formation
Capacity failure harms comprehension or learning

evals.prompt: Distinguish Cognitive Load Theory from context-management, prompt-craft, context-window, and compression. Give a mechanism-level reason for each boundary.
expected_elements: context-management owns retrieval and session working-set design
prompt-craft owns prompt tactic selection and wording
context-window owns token budget allocation
compression owns token-efficient representation mechanics
Cognitive Load Theory owns load diagnosis in authored or presented material

evals.prompt: A reviewer says, 'This skill is too long; remove the worked example.' Use Cognitive Load Theory to decide whether that is correct.
expected_elements: Rejects length as the only criterion
Classifies a useful worked example as germane or schema-building
Says to cut surrounding redundant prose first
Mentions that removing examples can increase intrinsic load
Targets extraneous load, not all load

evals.prompt: A dashboard widget shows 10 equally weighted metrics in one flat grid with no grouping. Apply Cognitive Load Theory and propose a fix.
expected_elements: Identifies the flat 10-metric grid as exceeding working-memory capacity
References roughly four independent chunks or chunk limit
Recommends grouping metrics into semantic clusters
Names chunking, segmentation, or schema-building
Does not simply delete metrics as the primary fix
